close_reason: Benchmark catalog, repeatability contract, schema checks, and exact quick commands pass
description:
## Objective

Make the benchmark suite complete, repeatable, and useful for comparisons without adding machine-dependent CI failures.

## Scope

Create one benchmark catalog under test/bench. Map each benchmark to its component, workload, limiter, profile, metric, and owner. Add common metadata and result schema checks for manual benchmark runners. Keep quick profiles in required offline checks. Keep standard, stress, and long comparisons opt-in.

Do not change lib or refs. Do not commit generated benchmark result trees.

## Acceptance criteria

- test/bench/README.md lists every benchmark family and exact command.
- Each family declares the component, workload, limiter, input size, concurrency, warmup, sample count, metrics, and supported profiles.
- Result artifacts include the Git revision, dirty state, Elixir and OTP versions, seed, workload, profile, and measurement units.
- Schema tests reject incomplete or incompatible result artifacts.
- Quick profiles have deterministic fixtures and bounded work.
- CI does not use a fixed wall-clock threshold across unlike machines.
- Repeated quick runs produce the same case inventory and valid result schema.
- mix test.bench exits with status 0.

## Handoff

Record the catalog, schema, repeatability evidence, commands, and any component with no useful benchmark in the completion comment.

comments.text: Completed in a613864 on main. Added test/bench/catalog.yml, the complete catalog README, and common Catalog and Result support. Eight benchmark families now declare a quality component, owner, workload, limiter, quick command, supported profiles, input size, concurrency, warm-up, sample count, metrics, and units. All JSON runners now record schema version, full Git revision, dirty state, Elixir and OTP versions, seed 0, workload, profile, units, and stable case IDs. Added quick/base/expanded ReAct memory profiles and a bounded quick default. Added schema rejection, catalog completeness, no-threshold, component-ID, repeated case-inventory, and decoded-JSON checks. mix test.bench passed 30 tests. Catalog/schema focus passed 6 tests. All eight exact quick commands passed. Repeated Action/Flow and AI quick runs returned identical case inventories; Signal inventory repeated identically with 150 cases. mix compile --warnings-as-errors, blocking Credo, formatting, and diff checks passed. No machine-dependent timing limit and no lib or refs change. Components with no useful benchmark remain represented by suite-wide proof policy and will be reconciled in U27.
